title: The rings
goals: Fly through the six rings in order.
starting_code:
# The pair of rings is written three times. Give it a name!
wizard.cast("drevo")
wizard.move_right(1)
wizard.move_down(2)
wizard.move_right(2)
wizard.move_up(2)
wizard.move_right(2)
wizard.move_down(6)
wizard.move_right(9)
wizard.move_up(6)
wizard.move_down(2)
wizard.move_right(2)
wizard.move_up(2)
wizard.move_right(2)
wizard.move_up(2)
wizard.move_right(11)
wizard.move_down(2)
wizard.move_down(2)
wizard.move_right(2)
wizard.move_up(2)
wizard.move_right(2)
wizard.move_down(2)
hints: Look for the four lines that fly through a pair of rings: down, right, up, right.
Give those four lines a name with `def` and put the four moves inside it.
Replace the repeating lines with a call to your new function in the three places.
intro: Here is my program for the long ring field! It flies through three pairs of rings. Between the first and second pair there is a clump of tall trees to pass below; between the second and third, a pond to pass above. The program is 21 lines long! Make it shorter with a function for the pair, called in the three places.
outro: Very well done! A shorter program is much easier to read, and it flies just as smoothly.
learned: Now you know that `def` gives some lines a name, and that the name with brackets runs them wherever and as often as it is written.
